Of Shinkansen passenger revenue of ¥548,260 million, ¥533,638 million came from non-commuter tickets (commuter passes: ¥14,622 million), and this depends on the number of customers on business and sightseeing trips. On conventional lines, the Kinki area (southern Kyoto Prefecture, Osaka Prefecture excluding some areas, southern Hyogo Prefecture, Shiga Prefecture, Nara Prefecture excluding some areas, and part of Mie Prefecture) generated passenger revenue of ¥318,012 million (commuter passes ¥108,973 million, non-commuter tickets ¥209,038 million), and the remainder was ¥81,691 million; the securities report explains that revenue in the Kinki area is affected by economic conditions, changes in work styles, and population trends such as the declining birthrate, aging population and urbanization, and that revenue on local lines is affected by competition with private cars and by regional economic conditions and population trends. In the fiscal year ended March 2026, use by customers for the Osaka-Kansai Expo and by inbound visitors was solid, and for inbound visitors the company released sightseeing tickets such as the 'WEST QR Kansai Area Pass'. Stores within station premises are operated by group companies that lease station facilities from the company, and station buildings and shopping centers include companies operating on station-premises land leased from the company, as well as tenants that move in. The securities report states that the company believes tenants prefer offices within stations and in their surrounding areas because of the convenience of location. In the Travel and Regional Solutions Business, revenue is also affected by the status of projects and contracted public work from government agencies and local governments. Because revenue from external customers in Japan exceeds 90% of revenue, information by region is not presented, and there are no counterparties accounting for 10% or more of consolidated revenue.

entries.39a5dac007b17c37: This is a reportable segment engaged in passenger transportation centered on railway operations, as well as station operations and other operating businesses, cleaning and maintenance, construction, machinery and other equipment construction, rolling stock and other equipment construction, and electrical construction. In the railway business, the company operates over a wide area covering 2 urban prefectures and 16 prefectures in the Hokuriku, Kinki, Chugoku and northern Kyushu regions, providing intercity transportation centered on Shinkansen and limited express services on conventional lines, and urban-area transportation centered on the Keihanshin metropolitan area and regional core cities such as Hiroshima and Okayama. In the fiscal year ended March 2026, revenue from external customers was ¥1,105,693 million, accounting for about 6-tenths of consolidated operating revenue of ¥1,845,840 million and making it the largest segment, with segment profit of ¥130,920 million, segment assets of ¥2,400,454 million, and capital investment of ¥196.1 billion. The annual securities report explains that transportation revenue increased because domestic demand remained firm even after the Expo, in addition to the Osaka-Kansai Expo and inbound demand, resulting in operating revenue of ¥1,105.6 billion, up 5.6% from the previous fiscal year, and operating profit of ¥130.9 billion, up 6.9%. The group also has 5 companies as units of management control — "Railway," "Sales of Goods and Food Services," "Hotels," "Shopping Centers (SC)" and "Real Estate" — which are a classification separate from the reportable segments.

entries.60c817b99a9b66ad: Operating profit for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥198,081 million (¥198.0 billion), an increase of 9.9% year on year, or ¥17.9 billion. Operating expenses rose 7.9% year on year, or ¥119.9 billion, to ¥1.6477 trillion, owing to increases in personnel costs and repair costs accompanying rising wages and labor unit costs, and the recording of Expo-related expenses, among other factors; growth in operating revenue (8.1%) slightly exceeded growth in operating expenses (7.9%). Non-operating income and expenses resulted in a loss of ¥14.3 billion and extraordinary income and losses in a loss of ¥4.7 billion; ordinary profit was ¥183.6 billion (up 10.9% year on year), and profit attributable to owners of the parent was ¥127.4 billion (up 11.9%). Segment profit was ¥130,920 million for the Mobility Business (operating profit up 6.9% year on year), ¥46,332 million for the Real Estate Business (up 19.1%), ¥16,264 million for the Distribution Business (up 17.6%), ¥529 million for the Travel and Regional Solutions Business (¥1,133 million in the previous year, down 53.3%) and ¥5,410 million for Others; profit in the Travel and Regional Solutions Business declined owing to higher costs and other factors. Rental profit on leased real estate was ¥54,765 million (¥46,851 million in the previous year). Among non-operating expenses, the most significant item was interest expenses, at ¥21.7 billion in the fiscal year ended March 2026 (up ¥2.2 billion year on year). Net cash provided by operating activities was ¥361.6 billion, net cash used in investing activities was ¥253.6 billion, and cash and cash equivalents at the end of the period were ¥234.8 billion. Total assets at the end of the fiscal year ended March 2026 were ¥3.9867 trillion, total liabilities were ¥2.6495 trillion and net assets were ¥1.3372 trillion.

entries.6e63b323ad9f9554: JR West Group is a corporate group that has railway operations as its core business, places 'safety' as its top priority, and expands businesses that make use of stations and towns. The business of the company and its affiliates (139 subsidiaries and 23 associates) is presented in the [[term:segment|reportable segments]] of the Mobility Business, Distribution Business, Real Estate Business, and Travel and Regional Solutions Business, and in Other, which is not included in the reportable segments. For the 39th fiscal year, there are 58 [[term:consolidated-subsidiary|consolidated subsidiaries]] and 5 equity-method affiliates. Consolidated operating revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥1,845,840 million, and revenue from external customers was ¥1,105,693 million for the Mobility Business, ¥285,762 million for the Real Estate Business, ¥232,641 million for the Distribution Business, ¥189,203 million for the Travel and Regional Solutions Business, and ¥32,539 million for Other. Segment profit was ¥130,920 million for the Mobility Business, ¥46,332 million for the Real Estate Business, ¥16,264 million for the Distribution Business, ¥529 million for the Travel and Regional Solutions Business, and ¥5,410 million for Other, and there is an intersegment transaction elimination adjustment of △¥1,375 million between these and consolidated operating profit of ¥198,081 million. The securities report explains that for railway operations, the company obtains permission from the Minister of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism for each line it operates, and after obtaining approval from the Minister for the upper limits of fares and certain charges, it sets and changes them within those limits. Safety is the foundation of management, and in light of the Fukuchiyama Line train accident caused by the company group on April 25, 2005, it is working to improve safety under the Anzen Kōdō Keikaku 2027 plan, which started in April 2023. The JR West Group Medium-Term Management Plan 2030, formulated in April 2026, sets 'Transformation into safe, high-quality and sustainable mobility' and 'Transformation of the business portfolio' as its basic policies, and designates 3 priority fields: the mobility field, the lifestyle services field, and the infrastructure solutions field. The securities report considers the progress of population decline and declining birthrate and aging population to be the 'greatest management risk,' and states that the company is especially affected by economic trends in the Western Japan region, its main operating area.
